stem:
Feroz looks at the diagram. Straight lines $\ell$ and $m$ lie on the same flat page and meet at point $P$.

Which claim correctly names the lines and the angle structure at $P$?

options.text: Lines $\ell$ and $m$ are intersecting, and their meeting at $P$ forms four angles.
Lines $\ell$ and $m$ can meet at two different points on the page if they are drawn longer.
The four angles at $P$ are what force lines $\ell$ and $m$ to meet.
Call $\ell$ and $m$ parallel, because they lie on the same flat page.

teacher.key_rationale: On one plane, two straight lines that meet at one point are intersecting and form four angles there. A second meeting point, reversing angles as the cause of meeting, or naming them parallel all miss that test.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source triangle rods as coplanar intersecting lines l and m meeting at P with four marked angles.
